configKeys.effect: Lets a Fire Arrow start a fire where it lands, exactly as a thrown fire charge would. With it off the arrow still burns in flight, still sets what it hits alight for five seconds and still lights TNT, campfires and candles — it simply leaves the ground alone. Only the block half is switchable; igniting on hit is vanilla's own behaviour for a burning arrow and cannot be separated from the arrow being lit.

events: net.neoforged.neoforge.event.entity.ProjectileImpactEvent (GAME bus, both sides, instance @SubscribeEvent method MoArrowsModule.onProjectileImpact registered by NeoForge.EVENT_BUS.register(this) in onInitialize; default priority NORMAL; returns immediately unless the projectile is an AbstractArrow whose getPickupItemStackOrigin() is fire_arrow and the hit is a BlockHitResult; places a fire block server-side and never cancels the event)
net.neoforged.neoforge.event.AddReloadListenerEvent (GAME bus, server; adds FireArrowRecipeReloadListener, which re-injects the shapeless recipe into the RecipeManager after every resource reload)

items.name: Fire Arrow
items.notes: FireArrowItem extends ArrowItem. Leaves the bow lit for 100 seconds (the Flame value), so it ignites what it hits for 5s through vanilla's own AbstractArrow.onHitEntity and lights TNT, campfires and candles through their onProjectileHit. On top of that the module places a fire block where it lands. Model reuses vanilla's tipped-arrow textures with a fixed ember tint; must be in the minecraft:arrows tag to be usable as ammunition.

notes:
WHAT EXISTS: one item, vanillaplusadditions:fire_arrow (FireArrowItem extends net.minecraft.world.item.ArrowItem), one shapeless recipe built in code, one item-colour handler, one event listener. No entity type, no renderer, no spawn packet, no mixin, no texture file.

THE ENTITY IS VANILLA'S. FireArrowItem overrides both of ArrowItem's factories — createArrow(Level, ItemStack, LivingEntity, ItemStack) for bows and crossbows, asProjectile(Level, Position, ItemStack, Direction) for dispensers — calls super, and then igniteForSeconds(100.0F) on the result. 100 seconds is the value a Flame-enchanted bow gives its arrows; no arrow stays airborne anywhere near that long, so the arrow is still burning whatever it hits.

WHAT COMES FREE WITH A BURNING ARROW (all vanilla, none of it re-implemented here): AbstractArrow.onHitEntity does `if (this.isOnFire() && !(entity instanceof EnderMan)) entity.igniteForSeconds(5.0F)` (AbstractArrow.java:378-379 of the 1.21.1 sources), TNT/campfires/candles light through their own Block.onProjectileHit, and water puts the arrow out — after which it is an ordinary arrow and lays no fire, because the handler re-checks arrow.isOnFire().

WHAT IS ADDED: MoArrowsModule.onProjectileImpact, on NeoForge's ProjectileImpactEvent (GAME bus, registered via NeoForge.EVENT_BUS.register(this) in onInitialize). It recognises the arrow with arrow.getPickupItemStackOrigin().is(FIRE_ARROW.get()) — the stack the arrow would drop, i.e. the item it was fired from; getPickupItem() is protected and unusable from outside, getPickupItemStackOrigin() is public (AbstractArrow.java:609). On a BlockHitResult, server side only, it mirrors FireChargeItem.useOn exactly: BaseFireBlock.canBePlacedAt(level, pos, direction) → playSound(FLINTANDSTEEL_USE) → setBlockAndUpdate(BaseFireBlock.getState(level, pos)) → level.gameEvent(shooter, GameEvent.BLOCK_PLACE, pos), with pos = hit.getBlockPos().relative(hit.getDirection()). The event is NOT cancelled, so the arrow still sticks and can still be picked up.

WHY AN EVENT AND NOT AN ENTITY: overriding AbstractArrow.onHitBlock would need a registered entity type, a renderer and a spawn packet for one line of behaviour. The event needs none of that and cannot desync.

TEXTURE — THE FIRST ATTEMPT LOOKED WRONG IN GAME AND WAS REPLACED: reusing vanilla's two-layer tipped-arrow model (layer0 tipped_arrow_head tinted, layer1 tipped_arrow_base) renders badly, because those layers are not cut the way the names suggest — tipped_arrow_base.png is ONLY the shaft and fletching, and tipped_arrow_head.png is the head PLUS scattered potion-drip pixels. The item now carries its own texture, assets/vanillaplusadditions/textures/item/fire_arrow.png, generated by scripts/gen_fire_arrow_texture.py from vanilla's arrow.png and committed, so the build never needs a client jar. The arrowhead's four greys (#FFFFFF, #D8D8D8, #969696, #444444) occur ONLY in the head — the fletching uses #E0E0E0/#C6C6C6/#3F3F3F and the shaft browns — so a plain colour table suffices with no positional mask; the script aborts if the source palette no longer matches. They map onto tones sampled from campfire_fire.png at the same brightness order: #F9EBAB, #EFCD56, #C96C03, #B13F00. On top of that the script glows three wood pixels of the shaft directly behind the head, and adds seven flame pixels (a tongue over the edge, a trail running back along the shaft) into cells vanilla leaves empty — 24 pixels differ from vanilla in total, the fletching and the rear shaft are byte-identical. The design was picked by the repository owner from six rendered variants (A nur Spitze, B kleine Zunge, C Fahne, D Vollbrand, E Glut im Holz, F Fackel); D is the one implemented. The script verifies all three preconditions before writing (head palette present, no unknown colours, every flame cell empty) and aborts otherwise. No item colour handler any more.

THE BOW TAG IS LOAD-BEARING: bows and crossbows accept ammunition by the item tag minecraft:arrows (ProjectileWeaponItem's ARROW_ONLY predicate). data/minecraft/tags/item/arrows.json in this mod adds vanillaplusadditions:fire_arrow with replace:false. Without that file the item exists but cannot be fired at all. It is the module's only dataGlob.

RECIPE: shapeless, one minecraft:arrow plus one minecraft:fire_charge, category EQUIPMENT, result one fire_arrow, id vanillaplusadditions:fire_arrow. Registered in code through AddReloadListenerEvent and re-applied on every server resource reload, like every other recipe in this mod — datapack recipe JSON does not load reliably here (see docs/modules/custom_crafting_recipes.md). The yield is deliberately 1:1; if a cheaper rate is wanted, that is the recipe's result count and nothing else.

CONFIG: MoArrowsConfig adds one key, `light_fires` (boolean, default true), checked at the head of onProjectileImpact. Only the block half is switchable: igniting on hit comes from the arrow being lit and cannot be taken away without taking the fire away, and the two effects are worth separating because laying fire is a ranged tinderbox in the hands of anyone who can craft the arrow.

NOT VERIFIED IN GAME YET (2026-09-20): compiles and passes Checkstyle; the client deploy was still pending when the module was written. Worth checking specifically: that the tint reads well in a hotbar, and that the fire lands on the face the arrow struck rather than inside the block.

NAME: the module id is mo_arrows ("Mo' Arrows"), chosen by the repository owner; the display name carries the apostrophe, which is why the build.gradle descriptor uses double quotes for it.
oneLiner: An arrow crafted from an arrow and a fire charge: it flies burning, sets alight whatever it hits, and starts a real fire where it lands — the part even a Flame-enchanted bow has never done.
recipes: vanillaplusadditions:fire_arrow — shapeless, 1x minecraft:arrow + 1x minecraft:fire_charge -> 1x vanillaplusadditions:fire_arrow, CraftingBookCategory.EQUIPMENT; built in code in MoArrowsModule.applyFireArrowRecipe and re-applied on every server resource reload
shortDescription: Adds the Fire Arrow: crafted from an arrow and a fire charge, it burns in flight, ignites what it hits and starts a fire where it lands.
